findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 11 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints '\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{r}(t) represent the velocity vector'. The subject is singular (one derivative), so the verb must be 'represents': '\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{r}(t) represents the velocity vector of the particle'. This is grammar only; the mathematics does not change.

Book correction: In the list after the drone's position vector the book prints 'y(t) = 2\cos t: north-south position'. The position vector it gives is \mathbf{r}(t) = 2\cos t\,\hat{i} + 2\sin t\,\hat{j} + 3t\,\hat{k}, so the north-south component is y(t) = 2\sin t; the book's own solution also uses it (its velocity has 2\cos t\,\hat{j}, the derivative of 2\sin t).
